pr_title: bluetooth: host: convert conn address on identity resolution
pr_body:
Fixes: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/61028

Fix an issue in the CCC configuration when the Peripheral device maintains two or more distinct connections on different identities with the same peer. The issue occurs when the local device performs the pairing and the bonding procedure on a connection associated with one of the Bluetooth identities. During the identity resolution, the peer address field in the CCC descriptor is converted from the RPA-type address to the Identity Address. However, the destination address on the remaining connection objects associated with other Bluetooth identities is not converted. Due to this, their CCC configuration is reset and GATT indications and notification fail to be sent even if the Central device subscribed to them.

Added necessary code to iterate over all connection objects during the identity resolution phase and aligned their destination address from the RPA-type to the Identity Address.
pr_comments:
> > when the Peripheral device maintains two or more distinct connections on different identities with the same peer
> 
> @kapi-no Could you elaborate on the use-case? I'm not sure this should be supported at all, given the headaches this kind of usage might bring.

The use case is one of the asset-tracking protocols based on Bluetooth - called Apple Find My, which implements its own Privacy solution instead of using a standardized Bluetooth Privacy feature. The Find My Identity needs to manage its advertising address (using the `bt_id_reset` function in the context of Zephyr API). Unfortunately, I cannot share any details regarding the protocol design as it is closed-source.

When such an asset-tracking protocol is combined with the main Bluetooth functionality, each functionality needs to have its own separate identity. Let's use an example of the LE Audio headphones with the location tracking feature (Apple Find My). In this case, separate identities prevent the location-tracking functionality from resetting the bonding information of the LE audio functionality during the advertising address updates with `bt_id_reset` function.

This use case is kind of similar to the HW approach where typically product has two different chipsets that require dedicated connections. In this case, however, we have one chip but the separation happens at the software level thanks to the dedicated Bluetooth identities.

Hi,

How does this comply with Core Spec 5.4, Vol 6, Part B, 1.1.1 "Permitted state and role combinations" ?

"The Link Layer may optionally support multiple state machines. If it does
support multiple state machines, then any combination of states and roles may
be supported. In particular, the Link Layer may be in the Connection State
multiple times with any mix of Central Role and Peripheral Role. **However, any
two devices shall not have more than one connection between them**."

> Hi,
> 
> How does this comply with Core Spec 5.4, Vol 6, Part B, 1.1.1 "Permitted state and role combinations" ?
> 
> "The Link Layer may optionally support multiple state machines. If it does support multiple state machines, then any combination of states and roles may be supported. In particular, the Link Layer may be in the Connection State multiple times with any mix of Central Role and Peripheral Role. **However, any two devices shall not have more than one connection between them**."

Well, the term device is not defined in the specification so it leaves some room for interpretation. If we understand the term device as device identity (identified by the unique Identity Address exchanged during the pairing), then this change is acceptable.

However, this PR does not attempt to change anything at the Link Layer level. It simply supports the Link Layer implementations (e.g. Zephyr LL, Softdevice Controller LL from the nRF Connect SDK) that interpret the word device as outlined by me in the previous section. If any of the LL implementations choose to discard the second connection with the same peer, my code won't do any harm to comply with this requirement that may be interpreted in a less favourable manner for the described use case.

Hi,

While I understand multiple ID usecase I have trouble understanding this patch.

Why all matching connections being updated on resolution and not just one that pairing was performed for?
What is more for those other conn bt_conn_identity_resolved() isn't called. 

I looked at test and I'm even more confused as this looks like pairing is expected to happen only on one connection while dst is expected to resolv on all RPA maching?  Are all updated connection now suppose to use same keys?

What if rogue device copy old peer-RPA and connect, will it be able to update dst (ID?) addr of other (yet to be paired) device?  This will prevent that device from properly notify on own addr resolution on pairing?

> What if rogue device copy old peer-RPA and connect, will it be able to update dst (ID?) addr of other (yet to be paired) device?

This is a very good question. I'll dismiss my review until this is answered.

After a second re-read of the bug report, I also tend to believe this is the wrong fix.

To me, it rather seems that it's the identities feature that is currently broken in GATT. Ideally, the CCC array would be virtualized for each identity. Since we don't have tests with that weird use-case (same peer, diff id) we never caught it.

@alwa-nordic and I have been thinking for a while that the identities abstraction is not well-suited to HCI, especially regarding privacy. And here we also see that it was kind of half-assed, as it should ideally virtualize everything about the host, eg. the name, the whole ATT table (at least the GAP characteristic which sets the bondable mode), etc.. for every identity.

It would be great if we had some usage data about identities, ie what people are actually using it for so we can figure out a better system.

> Hi,
> 
> While I understand multiple ID usecase I have trouble understanding this patch.
> 
> Why all matching connections being updated on resolution and not just one that pairing was performed for? What is more for those other conn bt_conn_identity_resolved() isn't called.
> 
> I looked at test and I'm even more confused as this looks like pairing is expected to happen only on one connection while dst is expected to resolv on all RPA maching? Are all updated connection now suppose to use same keys?
> 
> What if rogue device copy old peer-RPA and connect, will it be able to update dst (ID?) addr of other (yet to be paired) device? This will prevent that device from properly notify on own addr resolution on pairing?

Well, I believe that the Zephyr Host stack works this way right now. It performs address translation from RPA to Identity address upon successful connection. See in the `hci_core.c:bt_hci_le_enh_conn_complete` context:

1. `translate_addrs(&peer_addr, &id_addr, evt, id);`
2. `conn = find_pending_connect(evt->role, &id_addr);`
3. `update_conn(conn, &id_addr, evt);`

If the rouge peer copies the old peer-RPA, our stack will use the identity address in the `conn.le.dst` field for this connection object. The Zephyr Bluetooth stack worked like this before my change. My change simply maintains this convention in a case where we have two simultaneous connections with the same peer.

The attack you described is currently possible using a single identity and single connection flow. At first, the first peers connect to our stack using an RPA address that was observed by the rogue peer. The first peer pairs with our stack and disconnects. Then the rogue peer can use the observed RPA and connect to our stack. In this case, the `conn.le.dst` field will be populated with the identity address.

Non-paired connection objects on different identities won't use the same key objects. I simply wanted to use the same convention that was present in the Zephyr Host (we resolve the destination address of all connected peers regardless of their identity/pairing status).

Actually, my first attempt was to limit the conversion scope of CCCDs in the `convert_to_id_on_match` function (gatt,c) to the identity which triggers the identity resolution. However, I reached the conclusion that it will be inconsistent with the current approach of identifying the peers which is global and is not identity-based. I can go back and make a change in the GATT layer (gatt.c) instead of the SMP layer and the test will still pass. Please let me know what is your preference.

The only attempt of this PR is to fix the inconsistency between the CCCDs descriptors which are converted from RPA to identity address and the connection objects in which case only the paired connection object is converted. If you don't like the conversion logic for connection objects, I can limit the conversion scope of the CCCDs. Please indicate your preference.
Last force push: fixed typo in the test according to @alwa-nordic suggestion
Last force push: rebase on top of main; no diff has changed.
This PR is currently being discussed internally at Nordic and may be dropped.

issue_context.title: Bluetooth: Host: identity resolution causes CCC issues on other connections with the same peer
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**

The bug assumes that the application uses `CONFIG_BT_PRIVACY` and `CONFIG_BT_SMP` configurations. It also assumes that the application exchanges the Identity Address with the connected peer during the pairing phase.

When the Bluetooth GATT layer (`gatt.c`) gets notified about the identity resolution in the `bt_gatt_identity_resolved` function during the bonding phase for one Bluetooth identity, it converts the BLE address field (called `peer`) in all affected CCC descriptors from RPA into the Identity address:

```
for (size_t i = 0; i < ARRAY_SIZE(ccc->cfg); i++) {
	if (bt_addr_le_eq(&ccc->cfg[i].peer, match->private_addr)) {
		bt_addr_le_copy(&ccc->cfg[i].peer, match->id_addr);
	}
}
```
If another connection object associated with the second identity is connected simultaneously with the same peer, its peer destination address (`conn->le.dst`) is not converted from RPA into an Identity address. Once the second identity attempts to send a GATT notification or indication, it fails in the `bt_gatt_is_subscribed` function as the stack cannot find the CCC descriptor using the RPA address from the `conn->le.dst` field. The failure happens because of the conversion of the BLE address field in the CCC descriptor that was performed during the bonding phase on the first identity.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Create the Bluetooth sample with two Bluetooth identities and two advertising sets with the Privacy feature enabled.
2. Connect to the second identity and subscribe to any characteristic.
3. Connect to the first identity while maintaining the connection with the second identity using the same central device (with the same peer address) as the one used to connect to the first identity (e.g. the same smartphone).
4. Complete the pairing and bonding procedure with the first identity.
5. Observe that GATT notifications or indications fail to be sent on the second identity. 

**Expected behavior**

The identity resolution on one connection should not impact the CCC configuration on the second (parallel connections) even if you maintain two different connections with the same peer.

**Impact**

The Bluetooth stack fails to send GATT notifications or indications on other connection objects associated with the same peer address than the one on which the identity resolution and the pairing happened.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Linux
 - Commit SHA: the main branch (https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/commit/f16c4324a7e28c929f7226dd06fef87d951431c9)
comments: You might be able to work around that bug by unsetting `CONFIG_BT_GATT_ENFORCE_SUBSCRIPTION`

review_comments: Could you add a bsim test that exercises this part of the code? I'm fine with the current changes as long as they are tested.
Added a BabbleSim test as you requested
